title: Task-selected Fourier, spline and Chebyshev basis Views
hypothesis: A sparse Mirror code selects among shared Fourier, spline and Chebyshev basis families per task, preserving heldout forecasts with fewer active features/bytes than a fixed heterogeneous KARC bank and outperforming native basis-family selection.

world.teacher: each target is generated from one family; family ID known only through support examples

fresh.release_rule: Keep fresh sealed after native basis-selection alias or byte/quality gate miss.

controls: one fixed Fourier basis for all tasks
full heterogeneous KARC bank with native family IDs
success_gate: heldout nRMSE <=0.02, at least 25% fewer complete bytes and active features than full heterogeneous bank, strict quality/byte gain over native KARC family selection.
failure_gate: FAIL if native KARC basis selection matches Mirror or gates miss.
boundaries: Analytic synthetic functions only; no trained KARC/forecasting claim.
Family IDs are inferred from support but stored for inference; this does not test unknown family at deployment.
No fresh data after native alias or frozen gate miss.
